classification_scope: preliminary nonpublic; no primary-critical edition or manuscript collation
method: Read existing production English Qur'an text; compare identified passages in public Hebrew/English biblical witnesses; require editorial review for any public association.

entries.reason: Opening letter sequence and revelation claim do not establish a traceable earlier passage-level source.

candidates.evidence: Job 26:7 describes divine suspension of earth over nothing, and 26:11 speaks of trembling pillars of heaven; Qur'an 13:2 describes heavens raised without visible pillars, sun and moon governed by divine command.
candidates.difference: Job's image is suspended earth and pillars of heaven, not the Qur'an's precise formula; no proof of dependence.
candidates.witness: Hebrew Job 26:7 and 26:11 with 2023 Revised JPS translation; no critical apparatus reviewed

candidates.evidence: Both texts refer to divine ordering of vegetation and day/night.
candidates.difference: Genesis describes a sequential creation narrative; Qur'an 13:3 enumerates earth, mountains, rivers, paired fruits, and night covering day as signs. Not a distinctive passage-level match.

entries.reason: Neighboring cultivated plots, shared irrigation and different fruit qualities: no distinctive earlier textual source established.

candidates.evidence: Ezekiel describes opening graves and restoration to life; Qur'an 13:5 presents opponents questioning renewed creation after becoming dust.
candidates.difference: Ezekiel explicitly interprets the bones as exiled Israel and return to land; Qur'an 13:5 argues against denial of eschatological resurrection and adds punishment imagery.

research_note.title: Cosmology, cultivated land, and resurrection in Q13:1-5
research_note.chronology: Job, Genesis and Ezekiel are pre-Islamic biblical works with layered literary composition and later textual witnesses; no single manuscript date can be equated with composition. Precise dating and textual stratification require separate source-critical treatment.
research_note.textual_witnesses: Job 26:7 Hebrew/JPS inspected online; Genesis 1 and Ezekiel 37 references require original-language critical edition and version collation.
research_note.alternative_interpretations: Shared cosmological language may reflect widely circulating late-antique scriptural and poetic motifs. Ezekiel's national-restoration vision differs from the Qur'anic polemic about resurrection.

checkpoint.coverage_warning: Open PR batches are not canonical merged coverage; verify earlier gaps before treating 13:6 as globally next.
